VISUAL STORYBOARD · SCRIPT · ART DIRECTION

MODERN LIFE.
EDGE.

A monochrome product film that turns design values into physical metaphors: cosmic scale, human grace, balance, faceted precision, and engineered endurance.

01 / Creative idea

The visual system positions the faucet as a designed object whose edges, surfaces, and proportions deserve the same attention as sculpture or precision machinery.

THE CENTRAL THOUGHT

“The edge” is both a physical line on the product and a metaphor for being exceptional.

Each product claim is paired with a distinct image-world. Human movement signals elegance; suspended metal spheres suggest balance; a diamond suggests precision; gears suggest accuracy and endurance.

CAMPAIGN LANGUAGE

One object. One claim. One striking visual.

Keep the frame spare. Reveal the product with light rather than clutter. The campaign's short typographic claims become the narrative spine; the imagery supplies the emotion.

Format: 1920 × 1080, 25 fps, approximately 57 seconds.

Claim 02Elegance

Claim 04Precision

04 / Visual mood board

These reference panels are taken from the supplied ad and explain the image associations that give the campaign its visual identity.

COSMIC SCALE

Nebula texture, particles, architectural mass. A metaphor for presence and superiority.

HUMAN GRACE

Ballerina silhouette; clean arcs, controlled motion, high contrast.

BALANCE / TENSION

Polished spheres, fine suspension lines, repeated circles, measured movement.

FACET / REFLECTION

Diamond-like planes translate into crisp cuts and exact reflective geometry.

ENGINEERING MACRO

Dark gears and mechanical textures imply internal precision and durability.

PRODUCT / HUMAN GESTURE

The faucet profile and hand make a tactile, premium final statement.

05 / Color, material & finish

The ad is deliberately close to black and white. Tone, reflectivity, and edge definition do most of the work—rather than a broad decorative palette.

Void black#030405

Primary background / negative space.

Deep graphite#111315

Shadow detail and dark product planes.

Gunmetal#34383D

Mechanical surfaces and midtone metal.

Brushed steel#858C93

Soft reflected highlights; not too bright.

Polished silver#C8CDD2

Rim-light on the key edges and spout.

Porcelain white#F5F6F7

Typography and final logo contrast.

Product silhouette

Long horizontal spout, upright body, flat planes, crisp corners, and a minimal, architectural profile. Keep the shape readable before showing every detail.

Surface finish

Use glossy black or dark metallic bodies with narrow silver/chrome reflections. Reflections should describe the geometry—not turn the product into a blown-out white streak.

Material contrasts

Pair the faucet with faceted crystal, polished spheres, fine suspension wires, and machined gears. These are metaphorical visual references, not literal bathroom props.

06 / Lighting, camera & typography

Think precision studio photography with cinematic black levels, not a bright lifestyle bathroom commercial.

Lighting recipe

  • Near-black environment with deep negative space.
  • Use a narrow strip light to trace one edge of the spout.
  • Backlight silhouettes and use top spotlights for the dancer.
  • Use controlled grazing light to reveal metal gears and faceted surfaces.
  • Protect highlight detail; avoid wide, milky reflections.

Camera language

  • Slow reveals and still hero holds for product claims.
  • Macro sliders move parallel to edges and intersections.
  • Use a graceful, fluid movement for the dancer.
  • Cut on a shared line, angle, circle, or glint between metaphor and product.
  • Reserve fast rhythmic cuts for the internal-mechanism sequence.

Typography & layout

  • Light-weight, uppercase sans-serif with generous spacing.
  • Build copy as “EDGE OF” plus one larger claim word.
  • Place copy in a clear black region beside the product.
  • Keep logos white, small during the film, and dominant only on the end card.
  • Avoid ornamental graphics, gradients, and multiple competing messages.

08 / Sound design & edit notes

A practical recipe to reproduce the film’s restrained, high-end character. Treat these as recommendations rather than claims about the source audio mix.

Music bed

Minimal cinematic drone, low pulse, and a slowly rising harmonic layer. Let the campaign claims feel like chapter headings in one continuous score.

Accent sounds

Use a single metal tick for product edge reveals, muted suspended-sphere clicks for balance, a light crystal shimmer for facets, and restrained mechanical ticks for gears.

Transition logic

Match cut the dancer’s line to the faucet spout; circles to ripples; gem facets to product planes; gear teeth to machining detail. Let sound accents bridge the cut without overloading it.

09 / Production checklist

Keep the principles consistent across 3D renders, product photography, AI video generation, compositing, and final edit.

  • Lock the source product geometry and silhouette; do not invent new faucet details.
  • Keep the black background genuinely dark and preserve the shape within the shadows.
  • Use a small number of highly controlled highlights rather than global bloom.
  • Reserve abstract metaphors for transition beats; return to the actual product for each claim.
  • Make every claim legible on first viewing, with generous negative space and sufficient screen time.
  • Keep final KOHLER branding clean and centered, with no extra end-card copy.
